chains.name: Critical Chain: Remote Code Execution (RCE)
chains.description: The correlation engine identified a combination of findings that satisfies a predefined attack-chain rule. The presence of both Unrestricted File Upload and Local File Inclusion (LFI) may allow an attacker to execute uploaded files depending on the application's implementation and deployment environment.
chains.impact: If successfully exploited, this combination of vulnerabilities may allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code, access sensitive resources, or further compromise the affected system depending on the server configuration and application privileges.
recommendations: Break the chain by fixing the File Upload validation (use strict MIME and magic byte checks).
Fix the LFI by avoiding dynamic local file inclusion based on user input.

chains.name: High Risk Chain: Zero-Click Account Takeover
chains.description: The correlation engine identified a combination of Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) and insecure session cookie configuration. Together, these findings represent a potential session hijacking scenario.
chains.impact: If successfully exploited, an attacker may be able to capture active session tokens and impersonate authenticated users depending on browser behavior and application configuration.
recommendations: Implement the HttpOnly flag on all session cookies immediately.
Sanitize stored inputs to neutralize the XSS vector.

chains.name: High Risk Chain: Authentication Compromise
chains.description: The correlation engine identified weak password requirements together with the absence of brute-force protection. This combination increases the likelihood of successful password guessing attacks.
chains.impact: If successfully exploited, attackers may obtain unauthorized access through password guessing or credential stuffing attacks.
recommendations: Implement robust rate limiting and account lockout mechanisms.
